body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), uniformly over observed laws \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)\to1\) and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\Pr_P(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\). On \(\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\), \(b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))=o_P(a(T_n(P)))\) and \(a(\widehat T_n)/a(T_n(P))\to1\). Hence the eventual-regime analytic critical value \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\), built from the exact Palm-intensity expansion, and the canonical-simulation critical value \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\), built from \(n^2\) copies of the prescribed padded grid target, satisfy \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\) and \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\); both critical values equal \(+\infty\) on the vanishing complement \(\{\widehat T_n<T_0\}\).
body.justification: Pointwise pivotality does not remove the population-dependent number of effective LR opportunities, so the spatial clock must be estimated at the centering scale.
body.gap: Takatsu and Westling (2025) estimate ingredients for Gaussian uniform bands, and Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) study a pointwise isotonic scale; neither propagates a plug-in LR clock through Gumbel centering.
body.consumer: It turns the canonical law into a usable critical value without estimating tiny single-location tail probabilities from the observational data.

obligation.what_is_open: The calibration theorem awaits the canonical and causal-transfer limits, including random-horizon uniformity and padded-grid approximation.
obligation.obstruction: Relative clock consistency is enough for centering substitution, but it cannot create the missing Gumbel law or show that the finite padded simulation target has the same quantiles as the continuum maximum.
obligation.attempted: The inverse-centering mean-value expansion, scale substitution, and conditional empirical-cdf calculation for \(n^2\) simulations were completed. They close the theorem once the upstream limits are established.
obligation.partial_result:
The downstream clock calculus is complete conditional on the unresolved transfer.  The fixed lower bounds imply \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathcal V(P)>0\).  Hence \(\inf_PT_n(P)\to\infty\).  If \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)=1+o_P(1)\) uniformly, then
\[
 \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}=o_P(1)
\]
and \(\Pr(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\) uniformly.  Since \(\mathcal E_\star'(u)=\beta_\star+\gamma_\star/u\), the mean-value theorem gives
\[
 \frac{b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}{\mathcal E_\star'(\widetilde b_n)}
 \log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}=o_P(1),
\]
where \(\widetilde b_n\) lies between the two centerings, and also
\[
 \frac{a(\widehat T_n)}{a(T_n(P))}
 =\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}{\mathcal E_\star'(b(\widehat T_n))}\to1.
\]
Thus Slutsky's theorem would yield analytic calibration from the asserted Gumbel limit.  Conditional on the data, the Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz inequality for \(n^2\) independent canonical simulations gives an empirical-cdf error \(O_P(n^{-1})\); continuity and strict increase of the Gumbel limit would then yield the simulation quantile.  The missing premise is precisely the unresolved canonical and causal-transfer theorem, including random-horizon uniformity and padded-grid approximation.
